'''John Ralston''' (born 20 June 1946) is an Australian [[Physical chemistry|physical and colloid chemist]] with training in [[metallurgy]], whose research embraces various aspects of interfacial science and engineering.<ref name="Pearce2005">{{cite book |last1=Pearce |first1=Suzannah |title= [[Who's Who in Australia]], 1906-2006, XLII Edition |date=2005 |publisher=Crown Content Pty Ltd |page=1620 |isbn=1740950232}}</ref> He was made the Professor at the School of Chemical Technology at the [[University of South Australia]] (UniSA) in 1984. In addition, he was the Director of the [[Ian Wark|Sir Ian Wark]] Research Institute of the UniSA between 1994 and 2012.<ref name="JR.UniSA">{{cite web| url = https://people.unisa.edu.au/john.ralston| title = Laureate Professor John Ralston| first = Ralston| last = John  | author-link= | date = 2015| website = [[University of South Australia|The University of South Australia]]| access-date = 28 October 2023}}</ref> Ralston was awarded [[List of South Australian of the Year Award recipients|South Australian of the Year]] in 2007 due to his research.<ref name="AusIMM"/>

== Education ==
Ralston began his education in [[Melbourne]] at Christ Church Grammar School in [[South Yarra]]. He completed his High School Certificate (HSC) at [[Melbourne High School]] in 1964.<ref name="Pearce2005"/> Between 1965 and 1975, he completed his [[Bachelor of Science]] in Physical Chemistry (BSc<small>Hons</small>) and continued to do his [[Master of Science]] (MS) and finally his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]]; all at the [[University of Melbourne]].<ref name="JR.UniSA"/><ref name="Pearce2005"/> After this, Ralston studied and worked alongside other chemists at [[Swinburne University of Technology|Swinburne University]], [[Imperial College London]], [[University of Bristol]] and had a [[sabbatical]] at the [[Wageningen University & Research|Wageningen University]] in [[Netherlands|The Netherlands]] in 1979.<ref name="Zurich"/> Throughout the 1970s, Ralston studied in the [[United Kingdom]], until returning to Australia after being offered the post of Professor of the School of [[Chemical engineering|Chemical Technology]] at the then South Australian Institute of Technology (SAIT), the precursor to the University of South Australia in 1983.<ref name="Zurich"/><ref name="JR.UniSA"/>

== Career ==

=== UniSA ===
In March 1984, Ralston joined the [[University of South Australia|UniSA]] as the head of the School of Chemical Technology. During this time of work, he gathered further support and financial funds to expand programs and research for students at the University.<ref name="Pearce2005"/> He mainly concentrated his efforts on interfacial science and engineering, with an importance on practical actions in his research. This further research led him to gain the funding of a new research institute on the campus.<ref name="JR.UniSA"/><ref name="Data">{{cite web| url = https://researchdata.edu.au/lprf-john-ralston/184211| title = LPrf John Ralston| first = | last =  | author-link= Australian Government | date = | website = [[Australian Research Data Commons]]| access-date = 28 October 2023}}</ref>

Due to Ralston's work at the UniSA, the University has established the Ralston Medal for Excellence in [[Physical chemistry|Physical Chemistry]] and also the John Ralston Chair in Minerals and Resource Engineering for his scientific legacy.<ref name="Medal">{{cite web| url = https://i.unisa.edu.au/students/scholarships/prizes/unisa-stem/#:~:text=Ralston%20Medal%20for%20Excellence%20in%20Physical%20Chemistry&text=The%20medal%20recognises%20excellence%20and,physical%20chemistry%20which%20benefits%20industry.| title = UniSA STEM| first = | last =  | author-link= | date = 2015| website = [[University of South Australia|The University of South Australia]]| access-date = 29 October 2023}}</ref><ref name="JR.UniSA"/>

=== Wark Institute ===
In 1994, Ralston established at the UniSA, the Ian Wark Research Institute, in honour of [[Ian Wark|Sir Ian Wark's]] contribution to chemistry. Ralston would be its first director.<ref name="Data"/> Between 1994 and 2012, the 'Wark' Institute as it came to be referred to, endeavoured to research into minerals and materials used for the mining industry and also for other researchers in Australia.<ref name="Pearce2005"/> The Wark had a close association with the Industrial Chemistry Division of the [[CSIRO]] as well as the [[Australian Research Council]]. Over time, the Wark would come to employ over 180 academic staff and research students with an annual budget of [[Australian dollar|$]]20 million. These successes were due to Ralston's research as well as his networking with the mining industry and researchers at the UniSA.<ref name="AusIMM"/><ref name="JR.UniSA"/>

In the early 2000s, Ralston also established and became the principal researcher at the Australian Mineral Science Research Institute (AMSRI),<ref name="AusIMM"/> which attempted at further collaboration in [[particle science]] and engineering with the [[University of Queensland]] (facilitated by [[Alban Lynch]]) and with the [[AMIRA|Australian Minerals Industry Research Association]] (AMIRA) International (led by [[Jim May (chemical engineer)|Jim May]]).<ref name="Wark"/> Due to these collaborative initiatives, led by Ralston, the Wark received over [[Australian dollar|$]]200 million in grant funding from the Australian Research Council, as well as returning over [[Australian dollar|$]]1.5 billion in profit for the minerals industry, due to this research.<ref name="Wark">{{cite web| url = https://www.sapc.sa.gov.au/inquiries/inquiries/research-and-development/submissions-in-response-to-draft-report2/University-of-South-Australia-Future-Industries-Institute-Minerals-Processing.pdf| title = University of South Australia Minerals Processing R&D Real Value to the Resources Sector for More than 30 Years| first = | last =  | author-link= | date = 2012| website = [[University of South Australia|The University of South Australia]]| access-date = 28 October 2023}}</ref> Despite retiring in 2012, Ralston still partially works at the UniSA as an Emeritus Professor.<ref name="AusIMM"/><ref name="JR.UniSA"/>

== Honours, awards and fellowships ==

=== Honours ===
* 2001 – [[Centenary Medal]]<ref>{{Cite It's an Honour |ausawardid=1127562 |date=1 January 2001 |recipient=Professor John RALSTON  |award=Centenary Medal |access-date=28 October 2023}}</ref> "''For service to Australian society in colloid and surface chemistry''" 
* 2002 – [[Honorary degree|Honorary Doctorate]] at the [[Åbo Akademi University|Abo Akademi University]] in [[Finland]]<ref name="Director">{{cite web| url = https://www.unisa.edu.au/Student-Life/Support-services/Student-administration/Graduations/Ceremonies/Guest-speakers-and-honorary-award-recipients/2012/Laureate-Professor-John-Ralston-AO/| title = Laureate Professor John Ralston AO| first = | last =  | author-link= | date = | website = [[University of South Australia|The University of South Australia]] | access-date = 28 October 2023}}</ref>
* 2000s – [[Honorary degree|Honorary Professorships]] at the [[University of Tokyo]] in [[Japan]] and [[Tianjin University]] in [[China]]<ref name="Director"/>
* 2006 – Appointed Laureate Professor by the [[University of South Australia]]<ref name="Zurich">{{cite web| url = https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/matl/department/department/JohnRalston.pdf| title = Emeritus Laureate Professor John Ralston AO FAA FTSE| first = | last =  | author-link= | date = | website = [[ETH Zurich]]| access-date = 28 October 2023}}</ref>
* 2008 – [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] (AO)<ref>{{Cite It's an Honour |ausawardid=1138606 |date= 9 June 2008 |recipient=Professor John RALSTON  |award=Officer of the Order of Australia |access-date=28 October 2023}}</ref> "''For service to science and to scientific research, particularly in the field of physical chemistry and minerals processing, to education and to the creation and application of new scientific knowledge to industry''"
* 2012 – Appointed [[Emeritus]] Laureate Professor by the University of South Australia<ref name="Zurich"/>

=== Awards ===
